lines: Helping <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> speaks well of you. It does not erase everything else.
People are saying <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> came home because you stayed.
<aqua>{cured_villager_possessive}</aqua> cure changed the way people say your name. <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua>
You saved <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua>. I know. I just do not know what to do with both that and the rest.
People are saying <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> came home because you stayed.
<aqua>{cured_villager_possessive}</aqua> cure changed the way people say your name. <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua>
Are you the doctor who saved <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua>?
Did you really help <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> come back?
<aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> is better because of you, right?
The grown-ups said you are the wizard that saved <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua>. Are you really?
Did you really help <aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> come back?
<aqua>{cured_villager}</aqua> is better because of you, right?
The thunder <shake>shook everyone</shake>, but the village is still standing.
We are rattled, not broken. Count heads before counting damage.
The little ones <jump>jumped</jump> at every crack, but most doors held.
Lightning makes honest fear out of everyone. Thank you for asking.
We are checking roofs, bells, and nerves after that thunder.
The sky was <shake>so loud</shake>. I stayed near the bed and did not like it.
I think everyone is okay, but the thunder made my knees feel funny.
The grown-ups said stay inside. I stayed very inside.
I counted the booms and lost count because I hid.
Nobody should let the sky shout that much.
The <wavy>smoke</wavy> has thinned, but everyone is still counting what was lost.
We put out what we could. Keep water close until the smell fades.
Fire leaves more than ash. People will be <jump>jumpy</jump> for a while.
No one wants to say they were scared first, so I will: we were <shake>scared</shake>.
Everyone is checking walls, beds, and each other after the flames.
There was smoke and grown-ups yelling. I stayed low like they said.
I do not like fire when it runs around loose.
Someone carried water very fast. I tried to help by not being in the way.
The air tasted bad, but I think everyone found a safe place.
I am okay. My blanket smells smoky though.
The raid is over for now. Some of us are still <pulse>listening for horns</pulse>.
Everyone alive is accounted for, but calm takes longer to return.
We barred the doors, held our breath, and made it to the other side.
Ask again after the <shake>shaking</shake> stops. For now, yes, most are safe.
The bell did its work. So did the brave ones. The rest of us remember.
The bell was loud and everyone ran. I ran too.
I hid where I was told. I think that means I helped.
The bad people are gone, right? Please say they are gone.
I heard shouting outside and did not peek. Not even once.
My heart is still <jump>running</jump> even though my feet stopped.
The night brought trouble, but dawn found us still here.
We are checking doors and wounds. Night makes every sound <pulse>suspicious</pulse> now.
Some slept through it. Some will not sleep well for a while.
The attack passed, but people are keeping lamps lit anyway.
Everyone is quieter after a bad night. Quiet can mean alive, at least.
I heard monsters and pulled the blanket over my head.
Night was too noisy. I want morning to stay longer.
Someone told me not to open the door, so I did not.
I am okay, but I want the lamps left on.
The dark made <shake>bad sounds</shake>. The grown-ups made braver sounds.
